newsitem.title: THAILAND: Downgraded Thai banks generally trade steady.
newsitem.headline: Downgraded Thai banks generally trade steady.

text.p: Shares of three of the four listed banks downgraded by Moody's Investors Service on Wednesday were mostly unaffected by the news, traders said.
Only the price of Bangkok Bank Plc, Thailand's largest commercial bank, slipped two baht to 188 baht at 0526 GMT.
Other banks hit by the downgrade -- Thai Farmers Bank, Siam Commercial Bank and Industrial Finance Corporation of Thailand -- were all unchanged at 123, 137 and 70 baht, respectively.
Moody's said it had cut the senior debt and deposit ratings of these banks to A3 from A2.
"The prices of these banks were not affected much because investors had expected that Moody's would downgrade them. Investors have discounted the news," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit.
Brokers said only the timing of the announcement had surprised investors.
"Investors earlier thought that the announcement would come out in May. This is early," Bunsom said.
